items.title: Al Wynn Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: Oscar Young, he's a New Orleans boy, a trumpet player. He was very good. It was his band.

ctx.x: Well, some people were in fact, maybe others not. Can you tell me anything else about any other teachers you had or other trombone players you listened to? And maybe if you didn't study with them that you learned from them by...

Well, who has done more for me than anyone? Well, as I said, I was with Jackson for a few years, and he gave me all the fundamentals of things. But Preston Jackson was with the band. There was a place at 43rd and State Street upstairs. It was called the Red Mill. And, of course, I was on...it was just a dance hall. And it ran every Sunday. Every Sunday evening they would have matinee dances. And, of course, you couldn't get in there unless you had on long pants. Well, in those days, I mean, the boys, if you were…
Is he still around? No, he passed.
